accuracy.evidence: Homelands checked against the Inuit Circumpolar Council (Alaska, Canada, Greenland, Chukotka; about 180,000 Inuit) and the Saami Council (Sápmi: north Norway, Sweden, Finland, Kola). Qamutik, qajaq, qulliq, kamiit and two-layer caribou clothing checked with the Canadian Museum of History and Smithsonian Arctic Studies Center. Snow houses are framed as winter travel and hunting shelters, not year-round homes; the snow-house warmth claim is kept to 'can be above freezing', matching published interior readings of roughly −7 to +16 °C.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented stereotypes: 'too cold for people to live there' (step 0 prediction), Arctic vs Antarctica confusion (Antarctica decoy on the map and challenge), 'igloos all year' and 'only lived long ago' (myth sort), cotton being warm (clothing prediction and decoy), a high door to let heat out (igloo prediction). Adult text warns against Eskimo/Lapp and treating all Arctic peoples as one.

lab_distinct.evidence: The mechanisms are specific to Arctic life: tapping Inuit then Sami homelands around a North Pole map, dressing a figure for −30 °C with a warmth meter that rejects cotton and rubber boots, and building a snow house ring by ring where the door choice tests cold-air sinking before the qulliq lamp can be lit. Lab gate similarity under 30% against every other flag lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each task reveals the idea through feedback: a wrong land names whose land it is, each seal part explains its use (blubber to the qulliq), each clothing choice says why it traps or loses heat, the igloo refuses to light until the low tunnel is in and explains why, and the myth cards correct the stereotype with what is true today.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions each with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: 'too cold to live there' (map then shows six homelands), 'just the meat' (four-part seal sort), 'cotton is soft and cosy' (cotton rejected at −30 °C), 'door high like a window' (high door refused: warm air would escape).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions with tagged wrong answers; each tag has its own message: inuit vs Sami lands, Antarctica has no first people, layering is about trapped air not looks or weight, blubber was not waste or wall material, warm air rises so a high door loses it, reindeer dig for lichen not grass or fish, Arctic settled for thousands of years.

readability.evidence: Kid text FK grade 2.8 and adult 6.6 (limits 6.5 and 9.5). Short sentences, Inuit terms glossed once in plain words (qamutik sled, qulliq stone lamp, kamiit boots). Lab banners use one instruction each.

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate passed. Every kid paragraph carries a fact (where, how they travel, how clothing and snow houses work, using the whole seal, life today). Adult text is curriculum fit, checked facts and named mistakes, with no repeated template sentences.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 and desktop screenshots of every step after Show me (/workspace/wn-run-1116-1146/.tmp_run/shots, ar-*). Map land boxes are about 117 × 55 px on a phone with no overlap of the Arctic Ocean circle; clothing chips are full half-width 46 px rows; igloo status text wraps instead of clipping; sort boxes fill the width, and every action has a full-width button.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs passed on desktop and iPhone 13: all six tasks complete with Show me, challenge shown, axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in light and dark themes, no console errors. Buttons mirror every tap and drag (each land, each box, each clothing item, add ring / door choices / light the lamp). The canvas aria-label reads the lands found, the current card and boxes, items worn, or the snow-house state after every action.
